name: Snort 3 Fundamentals — Config, Inputs, Outputs & Rules
description: Snort 3 (Snort++) open-source IDS/IPS. Modes: passive IDS (read-only) and inline IPS (-Q flag). Architecture: Packet Decoder → Preprocessors (http/port_scan) → Detection Engine (rules) → Logging/Alerting. Config: snort.lua (Lua format), snort_defaults.lua. Inputs: -r (PCAP), -i (live interface). Outputs: -A cmg (alert+payload), -A u2 (unified2 binary), -A csv. Rules: added via ips{} block or -R flag. LibDAQ abstracts network data sources.
notes:
=== SNORT OPERATION MODES ===
Passive (IDS):
  → Observe and detect, cannot block
  → -r file.pcap    → reads PCAP (passive by default)
  → -i ens160        → listen on interface (passive by default)

Inline (IPS):
  → Can block traffic
  → Requires DAQ that supports inline + -Q flag
  → afpacket DAQ supports inline on Linux
  → sudo snort -Q -i ens160  → inline IPS mode

=== SNORT ARCHITECTURE ===
1. Packet Decoder (Packet Sniffer):
   → Extracts raw packets from network
   → Recognizes packet structure (Ethernet, IP, TCP, etc.)
   → Forwards raw packets to Preprocessors

2. Preprocessors (Modules):
   → Identify packet type/behavior
   → Examples:
     - http_inspect: identifies HTTP packets
     - port_scan: detects port scanning (thresholds + protocols)
     - arp_spoof: detects ARP attacks
   → Configured in snort.lua as Lua table literals
   → Empty table = use default settings: stream = { }

3. Detection Engine:
   → Compares each packet against ruleset
   → Match → forward to Logging/Alerting

4. Logging and Alerting System:
   → Records or triggers alerts per rule action
   → Formats: syslog, unified2, database

5. Output Modules:
   → Configured in snort.lua

=== SNORT CONFIG FILES ===
snort.lua (main config):
  → Sections: network vars, decoder, detection engine, dynamic libs,
    preprocessors, output plugins, ruleset, shared objects
  → HOME_NET = 'any'
  → EXTERNAL_NET = 'any'
  → include 'snort_defaults.lua'
  → Modules: stream={}, stream_ip={}, http_inspect={}, etc.

snort_defaults.lua:
  → Default values for all modules
  → Required by snort.lua via include

# Browse config:
sudo more /root/snorty/etc/snort/snort.lua

# List all available modules:
snort --help-modules

# View defaults for a module:
snort --help-config arp_spoof

=== VALIDATE CONFIG ===
snort -c /root/snorty/etc/snort/snort.lua --daq-dir /usr/local/lib/daq
  → Loads config, checks for errors, exits cleanly
  → Output: 'Snort successfully validated the configuration (with 0 warnings).'
  → Note: --daq-dir not required for just validation

=== SNORT INPUTS ===
Offline PCAP:
  sudo snort -c /root/snorty/etc/snort/snort.lua \
    --daq-dir /usr/local/lib/daq \
    -r /home/htb-student/pcaps/icmp.pcap -A cmg

Live interface:
  sudo snort -c /root/snorty/etc/snort/snort.lua \
    --daq-dir /usr/local/lib/daq \
    -i ens160
  → Default: passive mode; LibDAQ pcap DAQ configured to passive

=== SNORT RULES ===
# Load rules via snort.lua ips module:
ips = {
  { variables = default_variables, include = '/home/htb-student/local.rules' }
}

# Load rules from CLI (single file):
-R /home/htb-student/local.rules

# Load rules from CLI (directory):
--rule-path /home/htb-student/rules/

Rule file location: /home/htb-student/local.rules
Snort 3 rule syntax similar to Suricata; check:
  https://docs.snort.org/
  https://docs.suricata.io/en/latest/rules/differences-from-snort.html

=== SNORT OUTPUTS ===
# List available output plugins:
snort --list-plugins | grep logger
  → alert_csv, alert_fast, alert_full, alert_json, alert_syslog,
    alert_talos, alert_unixsock, log_codecs, log_hext, log_pcap, unified2

# Alert output formats via -A flag:
-A cmg   → fast alert + packet headers + payload (combines -A fast -d -e)
-A u2    → unified2 binary format (for post-processing tools like Barnyard2)
-A csv   → comma-separated values (customizable fields)

# CMG output example:
06/19-08:45:56.838904 [**] [1:1000001:1] "ICMP test" [**] \
  [Classification: Generic ICMP event] [Priority: 3] \
  {ICMP} 192.168.158.139 -> 174.137.42.77
  (then hex+ASCII payload dump)

=== STATISTICS OUTPUT SECTIONS ===
Packet Statistics: received, analyzed, allow, rx_bytes (from DAQ)
Module Statistics: per-module peg counts (HTTP GETs, TCP sessions, etc.)
File Statistics: file types, bytes, signatures
Summary Statistics: runtime, packets/sec, profiling data

=== LIBDAQ ===
LibDAQ = Data Acquisition Library
  → Abstraction layer between Snort and network hardware/software
  → Modules: pcap, afpacket, nfq, dump, ...
  → --daq-dir specifies where to find DAQ modules
  → afpacket: Linux zero-copy, supports inline mode

=== SNORT KEY FEATURES ===
  Deep packet inspection, packet capture, and logging
  Intrusion detection and prevention
  Network Security Monitoring
  Anomaly detection
  Multi-tenant support
  IPv4 and IPv6 support
